cells.tense: You are here with it now, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.ask: Once this week, catch yourself smoothing a story so it lands right, and tell the whole version to the person there instead.
cells.core:
You move feeling into meaning, and you do it out loud — something shared, something people can join. What you carry, they take up with their own hands and their own words. There's a picture of this going well: you say it once, plainly, and meet what comes back without rushing to answer it.

Where it bends is that you adapt the truth to the room a beat before you know you're doing it. That's not failure — the translation is work you're good at, and that's why it lands. What it costs is your dial: it gets harder to hear when adapting has turned into trimming. Staying here means the tuning has to know what it's working on. Feed it, and what you hand on keeps your shape in it, still yours.

cells.verb: carrying feeling into meaning people can actually join

cells.tense: You're bracing for a moment that hasn't arrived yet, and writing your lines for it now.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've been broadcasting and say it to a single person, in a room, and let their response finish it.
cells.core:
You keep saying what you know at a whole room at once. Ahead of you sits a version where they finally get it, and you're already living there — so any conversation can turn into a chance to convert. Broad-casting crowds out the back-and-forth. Sometimes this comes out as meaning people can take and use in their own day; right now it arrives as pressure, and the wide crowd it's aimed at is exactly the thing that makes it land flat.

What you're moving toward isn't more reach. It's one person in front of you, and one thing worth passing to them. The current you spend on the whole room is the current that's already yours to hand to one listener. A better sentence won't do it. Say the one you have to somebody who can answer.
cells.sheetLine: You're broadcasting at a crowd instead of handing it to one person.

cells.tense: You're still at a door that closed behind you, waiting for it to open again.
cells.ask: Tell one person, out loud, one thing that matters to you and where it comes from, and leave it without dressing it up.
cells.core:
The current is running, but it's not coming out where it could be met. A version of you is still at that door waiting for an answer. The meaning you carry has gone inward and quiet, so what reaches other people is flatter than what's in you — and you take that flatness as evidence there's nothing worth handing over. There is. It's just holding still.

The fix isn't more feeling poured into the spot that feels bare. It's structure: say one true thing to one actual listener and let it be imperfect. What you'd need to hand over is real; right now it's kept out of contact, and contact is what gets it moving.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped offering what carries meaning, not the meaning itself.
cells.verb: carrying feeling into meaning people can actually join

cells.tense: The pen is down, and you're already writing in a room you've stopped naming.
cells.ask: Name, out loud to one person, one thing you keep doing that quietly holds a group together, and say you chose it.
cells.core:
You already hand meaning to people — in what you make room for, what you let pass, what you keep going back to — and it reads to you as simply the situation. Nobody fills that role by accident; the shaping is running, and it's shaping the room you're standing in. The claim just doesn't come home to you. Sometimes you belong without dimming what you are; the bend is that the output keeps running without the credit, so you feel like a participant in something you're actually steering.

What changes it isn't more work. It's one sentence of ownership about a thing you did and would do again. You're already in the room. You've been calling yourself a guest in it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already shaping this group. You just haven't claimed it.

The ask survives being wrong: on Too Much it is one broadcast brought home to a single listener, on Too Little one real thing said to one real listener, on Balanced one place where the adaptation outruns the truth, on Unacknowledged one thing owned as chosen — all doable, finished, useful even if my read misnames their life.
